input.rationale: Open a first investigation of the InstallSnapshot resynchronization path on a follower whose own log already covers the index of the snapshot the leader ships. Read the snapshot-install tail, the cached last-log/last-snapshot accessors, the prev-log verification in appendEntries, the log-compaction helpers and the leader-side nextIndex/SEND_SNAP logic, then built one focused in-package probe (reusing MakeCluster/MockFSM/InmemStore/FileSnapshotStore) that drives a real three-voter history into that state and measures re-installs, the follower's applied frontier, its cached log claim and its store range, plus an untrimmed control. The experiment is requested from the controller for a retained receipt; local runs of the same harness were only construction feedback.

investigations.question: When a leader must ship a snapshot to a follower whose own log already extends beyond the leader's snapshot index (stale suffix, lower term), does the follower accept subsequent log entries, and does its advertised log state stay consistent with the log it actually holds?
investigations.hypothesis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot/config but never resets the cached last log entry, and compactLogs leaves the follower's stale suffix on disk (non-monotonic store) or deletes everything below it (monotonic store). Because getLastEntry prefers lastLogIndex when it is >= lastSnapshotIndex, the follower keeps advertising a log it no longer has, fails every prev-log check, and the leader can only retry the same snapshot (SEND_SNAP) forever: no entry is ever accepted after the install.
investigations.discriminator: Retained receipt of the focused probe: repeated InstallSnapshot acceptance (FSM Restore count rising while the leader's snapshot index is unchanged), the follower's applied index staying at the leader's snapshot index while the cluster frontier advances, and the follower's cached last-log index/term remaining beyond the installed snapshot index; the untrimmed control separates the snapshot-install trigger from the mere existence of a stale suffix.

knowledge.statement: The InstallSnapshot handler does not update the receiving node's cached last log entry (lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm). It sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot to the request's LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm, replaces the committed and latest configurations, and then either deletes the whole log store (monotonic store) or calls compactLogs, which trims only up to min(snapshotIndex, cachedLastLogIndex - TrailingLogs).
knowledge.conditions: raft.go installSnapshot (raft.go 1930-1977) reached by a follower for an accepted snapshot request; cache accessors in state.go 160-175; compaction rules in snapshot.go 217-279.

knowledge.statement: getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, and the snapshot's (index,term) only when the cached log index is strictly below the snapshot index. A follower whose cached log index is at or above the newly installed snapshot index therefore keeps reporting its pre-snapshot log tail as its last entry, both for prev-log verification of incoming AppendEntries and for the log-completeness test used when granting votes or pre-votes.
knowledge.conditions: state.go 160-175; consumers: raft.go appendEntries prev-log verification 1490-1516, requestVote/requestPreVote 1725-1748, AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog at 1445-1452.

knowledge.statement: Leader-side repair of a rejected AppendEntries proceeds only by decrementing nextIndex (bounded below by resp.LastLog+1), and setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound as soon as nextIndex-1 falls outside the leader's trimmed log store; replicateTo then jumps to SEND_SNAP, which re-sends the newest stored snapshot and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1. Repeating this cycle converges on re-installing the same snapshot index whenever the follower's prev-log checks fail at and above that index.
knowledge.conditions: replication.go 240-300 and 352-372; requires the leader's log to have been trimmed by a snapshot (TrailingLogs smaller than the gap), which is the normal steady state after log compaction.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.
Probe fields are read from the follower's cached state and its log store on the same process; the receipt is needed before treating the numbers as retained observations.

scope.description: Two real three-voter cluster histories in one process: a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is then restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. In the trimmed case the leader's log store is compacted to TrailingLogs=10 so it can only repair by shipping that snapshot; in the control TrailingLogs is large so entries alone can repair. Each case samples the victim's restores, applied index, commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range, plus the cluster frontier, for a 3s window with steady new writes.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced event is a full transport partition of one voter plus its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
The victim's orphan suffix is produced by real Apply calls it accepted as leader while partitioned, and it is kept because the restarted node replays its real log store.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds a test file.
Automatic snapshotting is disabled (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 1h) so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commits 60 entries, partitions the leader with c.Partition, fires 60 applies on it so they are appended locally without a quorum, waits for it to step down, shuts it down with Shutdown().Error(), waits for one of the remaining voters to be the only stable leader, commits 20 further entries, forces Snapshot(), records the snapshot and the trimmed store range, restarts the victim with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnects it to both other transports, emits ca_setup with the premise fields, waits until the victim's applied index reaches the snapshot index, then samples every 250ms for 3s while applying one entry per sample on whichever node is leader, and finally emits ca_probe with the raw values and derived booleans.
experiment.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded.

comparisons.description: Trimmed case: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window, while the leader's snapshot index is unchanged.
Trimmed case progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier even though new entries committed and were applied elsewhere.
Trimmed case: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term, and its store still holds that suffix.
Control: with an untrimmed leader log no snapshot is installed, separating the trigger from the existence of a stale suffix.
Control: the same cluster history without log trimming is repaired by log entries alone and the follower reaches the cluster frontier.

knowledge.assertion: the install path leaves the cached last log entry untouched
the stale claim is preferred over the installed snapshot
leader repair degenerates into re-shipping the same snapshot

result.summary: Repaired the rejected draft and resubmitted it. Changes: dropped the unsupported note fields from sources, corrected the state.go citation (file has 174 lines), widened the installSnapshot and appendEntries source ranges so each contains a verifiable Go declaration, replaced the requirement's anchors with three symbol-anchored declarations (installSnapshot, getLastEntry, appendEntries) resolved against the declared source ids, and removed the harness self-mapping from experiment.files. Read-only validation now reports valid with execution_requested: it creates the seven sources, three behavior entries, investigation @q_snapshot_install_stale_log, one interpretation and the two-case experiment (TestAssurance_StaleSuffixAfterInstallSnapshot plus the untrimmed control). Nothing else changed: the harness content, comparisons and the source-based defect account (a follower that accepts a snapshot while its cached last log entry is at or beyond the snapshot index keeps advertising that stale suffix, fails every prev-log check, and the leader degenerates into re-shipping the same snapshot) are unchanged, and the formal conclusion still awaits the retained receipt.
